data_objects.name: country_happiness_summary
data_objects.meaning: Country-level happiness scores, ranks, regional groupings, uncertainty estimates, and named score components.
data_objects.notes: The table does not state its reference period or document how the scores and components were constructed.

variables.name: Country
variables.meaning: Country name identifying the country summarized by the row.

variables.name: Region
variables.meaning: Broad geographic region category assigned to the country.

variables.name: Happiness Rank
variables.meaning: Ordinal rank of the country by Happiness Score, with smaller rank numbers corresponding to higher scores.

variables.name: Happiness Score
variables.meaning: Composite numeric happiness score reported for the country.

variables.name: Standard Error
variables.meaning: Standard-error estimate associated with the reported Happiness Score.

variables.name: Economy (GDP per Capita)
variables.meaning: Numeric happiness-score component associated with the economy and GDP per capita; it is not a raw GDP-per-capita amount.

variables.name: Health (Life Expectancy)
variables.meaning: Numeric happiness-score component associated with health and life expectancy; it is not a raw life-expectancy duration.

variables.name: Freedom
variables.meaning: Numeric happiness-score component associated with freedom.

variables.name: Trust (Government Corruption)
variables.meaning: Numeric happiness-score component associated with trust and government corruption.

variables.name: Generosity
variables.meaning: Numeric happiness-score component associated with generosity.

variables.name: Dystopia Residual
variables.meaning: Residual numeric component labeled Dystopia Residual in the happiness-score representation.

structure.description: Each row summarizes one country. Country is a candidate row identifier, while Region groups multiple countries.
Rows are ordered by ascending Happiness Rank and correspondingly descending Happiness Score.
The economy, family, health, freedom, trust, generosity, and residual fields form a family of named score components, while Standard Error describes score uncertainty.

uncertainties: The reference year or survey period is not declared in the table.
The score scale, normalization, weighting, and precise construction of each component are not documented by the evidence.
The Family label does not specify whether it denotes household family, perceived social support, or another construct.
annotation_notes: Semantics are grounded only in the declared train.csv evidence.
